title: North Sentinel: what to do if your engine dies
logline: Your engine dies at night and the current drags your yacht onto the reef of the one island on Earth you may not touch: here is how you survive without ever going ashore.
essence: Stranded at North Sentinel, you survive by calling for help and never going ashore.

hero.name: the sailor
hero.description: Series hero: solo sailor with a white round head and a red sweater.
hero.flaw: Alone and powerless: no engine, no lights, no way to steer away from the island.

hook.visual: Moonlit sea, the yacht dead centre with warm cabin lights; the engine sputters black smoke and the lights die.

core_question.text: You are stuck on North Sentinel's reef: how do you get out alive without harming anyone?

stakes.physical: Hull on a coral reef at night, waves breaking over the side.
stakes.legal_ethical: India bars approach to the island and contact with the Sentinelese; going ashore could kill them with your germs.
stakes.mortal: The islanders defend their shore with weapons.

spine.once_upon_a_time: A solo sailor is crossing the Andaman Sea at night.
spine.every_day: He trusts his engine and his lights to keep him safe and on course.
spine.one_day: His engine dies and the current drags him toward North Sentinel, the one island no outsider may touch.
because_of_that: Because of that, he hits the reef and is stuck within sight of a tribe that defends its isolation.
Because of that, he must call for rescue without ever going ashore, since even his cold could kill them.
Because of that, he stays with the boat, kills the lights and leaves nothing behind, as the Primrose crew did in 1981.
spine.until_finally: The tide lifts the yacht and he drifts out past the reef.
spine.ever_since: He knows the smartest way to survive North Sentinel is never to be there at all.

narration.text: Alone on a yacht, at night. And your engine just DIED.
narration.adds: the engine failure and that you are alone: the picture only shows a calm, lit yacht
the boat has no power at all, not just a dead engine

narration.text: And the current drags you toward one island. The ONE place on Earth you can't touch.
narration.adds: the current, and that this island is forbidden
the real name of the island

narration.text: The people here have refused contact with outsiders for thousands of years. And they defend that. Hard.
narration.adds: who lives there and that they refuse contact

narration.text: Then... crunch. You hit the reef. You're stuck.
narration.adds: you are stuck: the hull will not come off

narration.text: So what do you actually do? Step one!
Mayday! Grab your radio, channel sixteen, and fire off your emergency beacon. The Indian Coast Guard patrols these waters.
narration.adds: the radio channel, the beacon, and that the Coast Guard patrols here

narration.text: Step two: do NOT go ashore. Not for a photo. Not to say hi.
narration.adds: the rule not to land and the temptations to refuse

narration.text: They have almost no immunity to our germs. Even a common cold could be deadly for them.
narration.adds: why: their immunity, which no picture can show

narration.text: Step three: stay with your boat. And this has actually happened before!
narration.adds: stay aboard, and that it has happened before

narration.text: In 1981, a cargo ship called the Primrose ran aground right here. The crew saw armed islanders on the beach. So they stayed inside their steel hull for days. Until helicopters lifted every one of them out.
narration.adds: the 1981 Primrose precedent: the crew stayed and lived

narration.text: Step four: kill the lights. Stay quiet. Leave nothing behind.
And if the tide lifts your boat? Drift out past the reef, and get gone!
narration.adds: how to leave when the tide lifts you

narration.text: On North Sentinel, the only way to survive is to never be there.
narration.adds: the thesis: the only safe choice is never to go

steps.instruction: Mayday on your radio, channel sixteen, and fire off your emergency beacon.
steps.because: The Indian Coast Guard patrols these waters and can reach you.

steps.instruction: Do not go ashore, not for a photo, not to say hi.
steps.because: They have almost no immunity: even a common cold could be deadly for them.
The Primrose crew stayed inside their hull in 1981 and every one of them was lifted out.

steps.instruction: Kill the lights, stay quiet, leave nothing behind.
steps.because: You draw no attention and leave no trace on the island.

facts.claim: VHF channel 16 is the international maritime distress and calling channel.
India bars approach to North Sentinel Island (Andaman and Nicobar Islands Protection of Aboriginal Tribes Regulation, 1956) and the Indian Coast Guard and Navy patrol the zone.
The Sentinelese have rejected contact with the outside world and are thought to have lived on the island for thousands of years.
The Sentinelese likely have little or no immunity to common outside diseases; the exclusion zone is mainly a public-health barrier.

On 2 August 1981 the cargo ship MV Primrose ran aground on the North Sentinel reef; armed islanders gathered on the shore; the crew stayed aboard and were airlifted out by helicopter after several days.
An EPIRB emergency beacon transmits a distress signal via satellite to rescue services.

suspense_devices.desc: Fires light up one by one deep in the trees before the hero sees them and backs away from the rail.
The audience learns the islanders defend their isolation before the reef impact strands him there.
Radio and beacon are shown in step one; the tide that frees him is the payoff.
The Primrose: the same thing really happened here in 1981.

attempts.action: Flips the dead power switch twice.
Waits with the boat, dark and quiet, until the tide lifts it off the reef.

resolution.hero_action: He stays aboard, dark and quiet, then drifts out past the reef on the rising tide.
resolution.outcome: Free of the reef at dawn without ever touching the island.

overrides.reason: The threat is carried by the image and the overlay 'ALONE IN THE DARK' (threat lexicon: dark); the spoken hook lands on 'DIED' instead of a number.
The largest visual (the Primrose wreck at 0.62 D) is the proof beat of escalation 2; the midpoint turns on the ban-and-germs fact rather than spectacle.
Spoken re-hooks are sparse early; the 12-24 s and 25-40 s stretches re-hook visually (island reveal, fires lighting one by one, reef impact, beacon strobe) as planned in the shot list.
The recorded take delivers the 16-word hook at 3.57 w/s; kept for energy, the hook stays under 18 words and 4.5 s.
The payoff line is a fast release ('get gone!'); the slow, landed delivery is moved to the sting line that answers the core question.
Staccato fragments ('No lights. No power. Nothing.') pull the mean below 6; the one 18-word sentence is the island-reveal line and is split by a pause in delivery.
Second person is the frame for every step; third-person lines are the islanders and the 1981 flashback, which N-3 allows.
Numbers are limited to sourced ones (16, thousands of years, 1981); the 3-5 nm zone figure is deliberately not spoken because sources disagree.
Tension is carried by the delivery tags and the step structure; adding tension words would push the script past the recorded take.
The Primrose true story is the strongest surprise and is spent as the proof for step three; the payoff is the thesis line answering the core question.
'actually' is part of the series catchphrase ('what do you actually do?') used as the step-list opener.
The title carries the scenario in second person ('your engine dies'); the threat noun lives on the cover text 'ALONE IN THE DARK'.
Canon CAN-N2: the reserved narration gaps (7.6 s in total) lower the words/s over the span; the lines themselves still play at 2.6-3.0 w/s.
Canon CAN-N2f thins the narration so it does not lead the picture: fewer words than 2.83 x D by design, the gaps carry key sounds and the reserved close-up.
The hook keeps the recorded rhythm; its first sentence is 6 words.
Beats close on the next beat's first line so each gap stays in the beat it ends (canon CAN-N1).
